newsitem.title: CHINA: China's drought, floods seen due to strong El Nino.
newsitem.headline: China's drought, floods seen due to strong El Nino.

text.p: The unusually strong El Nino weather pattern has led to drought and floods this year in China and is likely to grow stronger by December, meteorologists said on Friday.

A drought racking northern China and floods battering the south were influenced by this year's El Nino, which may become the century's most powerful such determinant of global weather patterns, Ding Yihui of the State Meteorological Administration told Reuters.
El Nino refers to a weather condition caused by warming of water in the western Pacific ocean.
"Ocean temperatures went from cold to warm in four months," Ding said. "This is very rapid warming, and not often seen in history."
The strength of this year's El Nino had already equalled the century's most severe, which occurred in 1982, and it was not expected to reach its peak power until December, he said.

"The effect on crops will be greater in northern China," he said, referring to a drought that has hit a record 20 million hectares of arable land. Floods that have inundated 4.4 million hectares in the south were also linked to the El Nino, he said.
The phenomenon had weakened moisture-heavy monsoon winds blowing from India, trapping rains in south China while leaving north China hot and dry, he said.

Officials have said drought was expected to cut the size of China's corn harvest this year, although overall grain production was expected to be about 484 million tonnes, only slightly below last year's record 490 million tonnes.
"Overall, because we have not had too much flooding, this year cannot be considered a major disaster year, but the year is not over yet," Ding said.
El Nino's impact was normally stronger in the year after its onset, but forecasts on next year's effects would not be made until October, he said.

El Nino, meaning the Child Jesus, was a name originally given to the phenomenon for warm water temperatures around Christmas by Peruvian fishermen. It was later associated with abnormal weather around the world.
